llmlang.lockfile_builder.build.disposition: rewrote two 'refuses to write anything when X' bullets into checks-whether/if-yes structure, per the new llmlang-format.md §4c rule (condition leads, sub-bullet for the outcome, especially when several bullets describe alternative trigger conditions for the same action). No behavior changed.

llmlang.lockfile_builder.finalize.disposition: same restructuring as build() for its own 'refuses to write anything... when X' bullet, for consistency. No behavior changed.

llmlang.lockfile_checker.check.disposition: rewrote all seven finding-report bullets (TEST_LINK_MISSING through CODE_DIVERGED) into checks-whether/if-yes-or-if-no structure - they previously led with the result ('reports X when Y'), which reads as a flat sequence of facts rather than alternative outcomes of distinct checks, and phrasing was inconsistent (some said 'an entry', some didn't). The condition now leads uniformly in every one. No behavior changed.

llmlang.cli.load_config.disposition: same restructuring: 'uses X when given, otherwise Y', 'warns...when Y', and 'falls back...when Y' all rewritten condition-first with if-yes/if-no sub-bullets, matching the new §4c rule. No behavior changed.
